rv.q: It’s a tight and vigorous first half with some dark humour.
The intimate and breathtaking performances very naturally carry all the pain, toil and dejection of these lovely, accessible short operas.
For someone who does not regularly watch opera, this was a genuinely interesting evening and one that has left me wanting to explore the form further.
Bonatto’s double bill makes a compelling connection between two women pushed to the limits of survival and emotional endurance.
Her performance is heartbreaking, both musically and from an acting perspective.
This paring of Weill and Poulenc is bold and may not have paid off.
Unfortunately though, the stories of both pieces are a challenge to follow.

cn.t: This operatic double bill earns mixed reviews, with critics consistently praising Katherine McIndoe's strong vocal performance but finding the pairing of Weill and Poulenc works bold yet uneven, lacking sufficient context.
